title: Which expression gives the thickness after ten folds?
description: A sheet of thickness v is folded ten times, and the right expression is picked from six choices. Then four plus four plus four is compared with four times four times four. Keeko's doubt is that ten folds give v added ten times.
teaching_notes: One idea: repeated adding is a multiplication, but repeated multiplying is a power, and each fold multiplies by two. Watch for students who think ten folds give ten times the thickness.

source: A sheet has thickness v. Which expression gives its thicknes
video_script.why: The child can write the thickness after a few folds and now writes it for ten folds with a letter, and tells repeated adding from repeated multiplying.
video_script.substitution: The book's own letter v for the thickness of the sheet, and the book's own four plus four plus four against four times four times four.
video_script.anchor: a sheet of thickness v drawn side on, with the six choices of the book beside it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks ten folds give v added ten times, like ten sheets stacked. A fold doubles the layers, so the thickness is multiplied by two for every fold.
video_script.payoff_line: After ten folds, the thickness is two to the power ten, multiplied by v

final_answer.spoken: two to the power ten, multiplied by v; and four plus four plus four is twelve while four times four times four is sixty four

maths_rules: 10v and 10 + v and 2 × 10 × v use 10 only once; 2¹⁰ has no v; 10²v = 100v
slip: 10v is v added ten times
video_script.design: One idea: each fold multiplies by two, so ten folds multiply by ten twos. The sheet and the six choices stay all video; wrong choices are greyed out one by one; one slip at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, rule out the other choices.

<bookmark mark='nov'/>Two to the power ten has no v.
<bookmark mark='hundred'/>Ten squared v is one hundred v.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, compare repeated adding with repeated multiplying.
Four plus four plus four is three times four.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Four times four times four is four to the power three.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Four times four is sixteen, and sixteen times four is left to find.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: ten single sheets stacked appear and are crossed out; the layers double on each of the ten folds

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ten folds give v added ten times, like ten single sheets stacked.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But each fold doubles the layers, it does not add one more sheet.
The thickness is multiplied by two, ten times over.
